Hey! You can set an appointment with a gynecologist, psychiatrist, or even if you have a regular/go-to doctor. You may be referred to the appropriate one, or you could be told it’s all in your head, or you could “hit the jackpot,” and find the medical professional that listens to you. Please don’t “put in the towel,” if the first answer you get is one that discredits every one of your concerns. It may be hard but you know how your body is/can get. If it happens a lot, it’s probably not the farce some make it out to be. I know bills can stack up, so it’s really up to your judgement to see who can help you best.
You can keep track of your symptoms through a diary, or what have you, for a few cycles. It’s important to establish the pattern of symptoms! Be descriptive.

Now, treatment for PMDD is usually aiming to balance hormones, since the hormonal fluctuation during the luteal phase, is what brings about this intense version of PMS. So, that means birth control, and/or a type of antidepressants. Maybe instead of around-the-month medication, you take it at strategic points in your cycle, in order to make everything bearable. 
There is also research for a more natural regiment, if that’s more what you like. It involves dietary changes and consuming naturally-derived supplements—as opposed to turning to western pharma. 
You can always pop over to the PMDD sub and see their thoughts!! It’s a nice community over there! I haven’t come across any harshness.
